scenario: [LUNI.2.4.1], with [LUNI.2.4]: a Rational of any size is exact at compile time, and only a constant the compiler emits is held to a runtime value's range. The standard library's `kiloparsec` is `x * 3.085677581491367e19` m, whose exact numerator is past 2^63 - 1; `electronvolt` (`x * 1.602176634e-19` J) and `dalton` (`x * 1.66053906660e-27` kg) have exact denominators past it. All three are `float64` dimensions, so each emits `a` as a `Float`, which is finite and not zero. Each is used in a `where`: a `length` slot against `1_kiloparsec`, an `electronvolt` slot against `1_electronvolt`, a `mass` slot against `1_dalton`. It compiles. A compiler that bounds the Rational's parts at int64 refuses the standard library. PATH PINNED: `dsc.validate.luni_2_4_1_unit_constants` (through `dsc.quantity.luni_2_4_1_unit_out_of_range`) and `dsc.typecheck.luni_3_1_7_literal_type` (through `dsc.quantity.luni_2_4_1_literal_out_of_range`) passing each, through `dsc.exact.to_float`.
rules_ds:
from units.astro import kiloparsec
from units.metric import electronvolt, dalton

schema Body scope logical:
    id: String key
    d: length mutable
    e: electronvolt mutable
    m: mass mutable

rule far:
    Body b where b.d > 1_kiloparsec
->
    log info "far"

rule charged:
    Body b where b.e > 1_electronvolt
->
    log info "charged"

rule heavy:
    Body b where b.m > 1_dalton
->
    log info "heavy"
